Can I get access too? <@!689161464829050960> unfortunately, the access is kind of crude: it's basically read/write/admin It's strange but I do not have *Owner* permissions to https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs repo any more. So. I may not be able to grant permission. But I think Triage permission would be good to assign issues/PRs on the eth1.0-specs repo. <@!552133098075193354> could you look into it? so to assign issues/PRs, I believe you need the same rights as to merge them I suppose *Triage* permission will help We need Github enterprise for that 😦 We don't have it for /ethereum, but I can enquire about it Given that, I'm a bit reluctant of giving contributors merge rights until they've been involved for a while (e.g. Pooja, Sam, Lightclient) Jeez, that's a paid feature? Following up with some more maths: if `TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_SYNC_SUBCOMMITTEE` were increased to 8 this would result in around a 96% chance that there are aggregator for all subnets in an epoch, however over the period of a day it is still pretty much guaranteed that there will be at least one subcommittee without aggregators. If `TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_SYNC_SUBCOMMITTEE` were increased to 16 that would pretty much solve the problem, but obviously then we're at a 1 in 8 chance of a sync committee member being an aggregator so a fair bit more overhead. I would have preferred it if aggregators weren't rotated quite as quickly as every slot, but still think that the overhead of increasing `TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_SUNC_SUBCOMMITTEE` to 16 is going to be worthwhile in terms of the level of surety that sync committee messages will be included on the chain (or at least have a fighting chance of doing so). <@!291925846556540928> thoughts on this? I'll review this after acd 🙏

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
Following up with some more maths: if `TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_SYNC_SUBCOMMITTEE` were increased to 8 this would result in around a 96% chance that there are aggregator for all subnets in an epoch, however over the period of a day it is still pretty much guaranteed that there will be at least one subcommittee without aggregators.  If `TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_SYNC_SUBCOMMITTEE` were increased to 16 that would pretty much solve the problem, but obviously then we're at a 1 in 8 chance of a sync committee member being an aggregator so a fair bit more overhead.

I would have preferred it if aggregators weren't rotated quite as quickly as every slot, but still think that the overhead of increasing `TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_SUNC_SUBCOMMITTEE` to 16 is going to be worthwhile in terms of the level of surety that sync committee messages will be included on the chain (or at least have a fighting chance of doing so).

<@!291925846556540928> thoughts on this?
